we construct a Sigma-protocol for a list of N commitments having one commitment opening to 0, where the prover only needs to know an opening of the commitment that opens to zero, and where the proof requires the transmission of a small number of commitments.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to construct a proof system for a list of n commitments, such that the prover only knows one opening.
the following question: How to prove that one element of a list is zero?
the following question: Is there an efficient way to convince a verifier that a given list of commitments has at least one opening to 0, without revealing the index of the opening?

the prover can convince the verifier to believe that the prover knows a secret and can spend a coin without knowing the secret and without being able to spend the coin.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a Sigma-protocol for a list of n commitments, of which one has to be 0, that is, we prove one-out-of-many properties.
we construct a Sigma-protocol for the language of lists having a zero.
we construct an efficient Sigma-protocol that is zero-knowledge, special honest verifier, and one-out-of-many proofs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a Sigma-protocol can be designed for a set of commitments without the knowledge of openings of all the commitments in the set, as long as the set has a single commitment that opens to a fixed value (e.g., 0).
Sigma-protocols can tolerate a large number of commitments without requiring the prover to have openings for all of them.
Sigma-protocols for the discrete logarithm problem can be extended to prove that a list of commitments has at least one commitment opening to 0.
